study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized cerebellar damage predicts the presence of behavioral disorders in children with brainstem tumors

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to establish normative models for 26 cerebellar regions. GPR is a Bayesian non-parametric modeling approach that considers prediction uncertainty and provides probability distributions for predicted values. Models were initially estimated with 10-fold cross-validation on healthy children data.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Using volumetric data from the 26 cerebellar regions, we established normative models with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), incorporating age and gender as covariates. This Bayesian non-parametric modeling approach inherently considers prediction uncertainty and provides probability distributions for predicted values.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cerebellar lobule volumes for 26 regions were used as response variables. The regions included left and right lobules I-III, IV, V, VI, VIIB, VIII, IX, X, Crus I, Crus II, vermis lobules VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, and corpus medullare. ACAPULCO (Automatic Cerebellum Anatomical Parcellation using U-Net with Locally Constrained Optimization) was used for cerebellar segmentation.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: we obtained volumes for 28 cerebellar regions, including left and right lobules I-III, IV, V, VI, VIIB, VIIIA, VIIIB, IX, X, Crus I, Crus II, and vermis lobules VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, and corpus medullare. Due to inconsistent boundaries between lobules VIIIA and VIIIB, these regions were merged into single lobules VIII for the left and right sides, respectively. This workflow ultimately yielded volume measurements for 26 cerebellar lobules

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and gender (sex) were used as covariates in the GPR normative models. The study noted this as a limitation, acknowledging that education and home environment were not included.
